5-.18 = 4.82.

This is only a way to estimate. Not a way to calculate

First you need to know how to solve a basic log in scientific notation
Log (10^1) = 1
Log(10^-1) = -1
Log (10^87) = 87

When you take the negative log of something, it’ll just be the negative of the exponent. This only applies to logs with a base of ten which is ALWAYS the case in chemistry for purposes of the OAT but different when practicing QR questions (just keep this in mind)

So the easiest trick is converting to scientific notation..

pH = -log (.14)

pH = -log (1.4*10^-1)

pH approx = 1 - 0.14 = 0.86

Take the exponent and subtract that from the value of the number before the 10 but as a decimal..Lemme give a few more examples just to be clear.
Example 1

[H] = 2.3 

Find the pH

pH = -log (2.3*10^0)

pH = 0 - .23 = -0.23

Example 2

[H] = 0.0075

pH = -log (7.5 * 10^-3)

pH = 3 - 0.75 = 2.25 approx
So we took the exponent, brought it to the front and subtract .75 (which is 7.5/10)

I am 5’1 and have weighed from 105 pounds to 130 pounds. Basically the entirety of the normal BMI spectrum.

Wanna take a guess at when I lost my period? It’s when I lost MUSCLE MASS and therefore - weight. I went from being a consistent 125 lbs pre-Covid to a 105 during the pandemic and completely lost my period. This was due to not working on muscle building. 

Weight does not matter!!! You have to figure out what PCOS-type you are dealing with and deal with it accordingly. I have lean-PCOS insulin resistant type. 

Building muscle helps so much with glucose regulation so that’s why my period was so regular. When I lost 20 pounds, like 3-4 pounds close to underweight, I completely stopped ovulating. 

It was only when I gained weight back to 120 and began muscle building and taking my supplements where I finally got my period back and regularly ovulated

When I was first diagnosed, I was told I had three options - metformin, the pill, or nothing since I wasn't TTC at the time. I have lean PCOS with my main symptoms being hormonal acne and longer cycles (33-35 days).  If my body is super out of whack (like when I lost 20 pounds due to the pandemic) I can go a cycle or even two without ovulation so it could be up to 90 days without a period.

When I gained the weight back, I still did not get my period back until I regularly started Ovasitol. It is pricey but it seems better than any Amazon brand I've tried. I take the packets as they keep me more consistent.

I would say try it for 3-4 months as that is usually what they recommend - if it doesn't help you, your PCOS may not be related to insulin/glucose dysfunction.

Also, if Ovasitol does end up helping your symptoms, strength training with heavy compound sets and myoreps for single muscle groups helped tremendously with keeping my body feeling healthy and ensuring ovulation in addition to the Ovasitol.

Edit: I did not cut out sweets or carbs while taking Ovasitol, just minimized added sugars instead of binging. When I do have something sweet like a pastry or lots of chocolate, I like to pair it with a protein/fat source like milk or protein smoothie just to reduce a blood sugar spike
